findings.reason: The parser removes empty operands before validating the expression, so malformed authorization requirements with a nonempty operand still succeed. For example, parse('reports.view.team & ') returns a single-capability requirement instead of rejecting the missing conjunct. This is fail-open behavior because the malformed expression is normalized into a weaker requirement.

evidence.detail: array_filter discards empty & clauses and validation only checks whether every clause was removed; with reports.view.team &, one clause remains and is returned as TYPE_SINGLE. parseClause applies the same pattern to | operands.

findings.remediation: Validate every token before filtering, rejecting an expression when any & clause or | operand is empty after trimming. Preserve filtering only after successful validation, or avoid filtering entirely.
findings.regressionTest: Add cases asserting InvalidArgumentException for leading, trailing, and repeated operators, including & cap, cap &, cap1 && cap2, | cap, cap |, and cap1 || cap2.

coverage: Updated unit tests and hash-bound red/green evidence
